context: Tech demo showcasing quadtree nearest-neighbor detection — interactive scatter plot where hovering finds the 10 closest particles, with zoom and optional Voronoi overlay
first_impression: Polished and deliberate: a clean white canvas with a well-chosen Tol qualitative palette, subtle glow-ring highlights, and dashed connector lines that make the nearest-neighbor mechanic immediately legible.
what_works: Intentional Paul Tol bright palette instead of default schemeCategory10 shows real color awareness; interaction design is layered and satisfying — glow rings, dashed connectors, crosshair, and Voronoi toggle all reinforce the quadtree concept without cluttering the canvas.
what_doesnt: The legend and title-bar both anchor top-left and compete spatially — the title sits at y=40px directly below a wrapping legend, creating a cramped header zone that overlaps the top-left particle cluster; typographic hierarchy is minimal, with legend labels, subtitle, and info bar all rendered at 12px system-ui with only color differentiating them.
